newsitem.title: USA: Brunswick to buy Life Fitness for $310 mln.
newsitem.headline: Brunswick to buy Life Fitness for $310 mln.

text.p: Brunswick Corp said Wednesday it signed an agreement to buy Life Fitness for approximately $310 million from a private equity fund managed by Mancuso & Co.

Life Fitness manufactures computerized cardiovascular and strength training fitness equipment for health clubs and other facilities and the high-end consumer markets. Its products include the Lifecycle stationary bicycle.
Life Fitness has annual sales of approximately $180 million. Life Fitness also markets treadmills, stairclimbers, rowers, cross trainers and strength training equipment to fitness centers world wide.
Completion of the acquisition is subject to customary conditions, and the transaction is scheduled to close in July. The business will continue to be operated by its current management.

"Life Fitness fits perfectly with the strategy Brunswick is executing," said Chairman Peter Larson said in a statement. "We have targeted the active recreation segment due to favorable demographic and consumer trends, such as baby boomers remaining more active as they move into their 50's with more spendable income and the emphasis on wellness, active life styles and social interaction."
He said Brunswick also sees growth opportunities for Life Fitness in the wellness market, as physicians promote exercise to treat and reduce the risk of disease, and also in international markets.

"Becoming a part of Brunswick's growing family of active recreation products is a tremendous opportunity for Life Fitness," Life Fitness President Augie Nieto said in a statement. "Both companies share a strong belief in serving the needs of its customers, and Brunswick is committed to supporting the ongoing investments in product innovation that are critical to Life Fitness continuing its global leadership position."
Brunswick serves the outdoor and indoor active recreation market.
